events_seen: WAIVER CLAIM (Oct 16 (today)): Kevin added Jahan Dotson (WR, ATL).
WAIVER CLAIM (Oct 14 (2 days ago)): Drew added Brandin Cooks (WR, SF) (dropped Joe Mixon (RB, FA)).
WAIVER CLAIM (Oct 13 (3 days ago)): Wingard added Corey Kiner (RB, NE) for $9 FAAB (dropped DeeJay Dallas (RB, MIN)).
FREE AGENT ADD (Oct 11 (5 days ago)): Ryan added Jalen Brooks (WR, ARI) (dropped Odell Beckham (WR, MIN)).
FREE AGENT ADD (Oct 10 (6 days ago)): Ryan added Odell Beckham (WR, MIN) (dropped Demarcus Robinson (WR, SF)).
FREE AGENT ADD (Oct 10 (6 days ago)): Charles added Roschon Johnson (RB, CHI).
WAIVER CLAIM (Oct 08 (8 days ago)): Mitchum added Dameon Pierce (RB, PHI) for $1 FAAB (dropped Jacob Cowing (WR, SF)).

WEEK 5 RESULTS: Corbishley def. Jake, 145.9-124.3; Shaq def. Adam, 112.0-99.9; Fronge def. Drew, 158.0-94.0 (BLOWOUT); Charles def. Mitchum, 201.4-105.1 (BLOWOUT); Kevin def. Brent, 150.1-146.2 (NAIL-BITER); Ryan def. Wingard, 174.4-87.9 (BLOWOUT)

tweets.name: Marty Volkman
tweets.text: BREAKING: Kevin adds Jahan Dotson off waivers today. RDC already at 7-3, now adding WR depth mid-week before a matchup against Wingard. The floor at Redline keeps rising.

tweets.name: Vivienne Ashcroft
tweets.text: Charles put up 201.4 points last week against Mitchum. The Ledger has been tracking CROWN's scoring pace all season and I will say plainly: we have not seen a floor like this from any franchise in this league's short history. The board agrees — $146.42 and still the market-cap leader.

tweets.name: Vance Hollis
tweets.text: CORBISHLEY IS UP 30.9-4.4 ON FRONGE AND I NEED EVERYONE TO UNDERSTAND THAT APEX IS PLAYING LIKE A TEAM THAT LOST A CHAMPIONSHIP FINAL AND CAME BACK ANGRIER. SIXTEEN TRADES LAST OFFSEASON. THIS IS WHAT THAT BUYS YOU.

tweets.name: Terrence E. Odom
tweets.text: People want to talk about my 5-7 record but nobody wants to talk about the fact that Kevin surviving a 150-point nail-biter then immediately going out and claiming Jahan Dotson is exactly the kind of quiet move that wins leagues in December. I see things early. That is the framework.

tweets.name: Jay Kelpey
tweets.text: Buddy, Terrence is 5-7 and just used the word 'framework' again. At some point the framework has to produce correct picks. That is, I believe, the entire premise of a pick-em competition.

tweets.name: Bo Ruckman
tweets.text: 8-4, locks 2-0, and I have a Corbishley-Fronge live game sitting at 30.9-4.4 in the first window that I picked correctly. I am not going to make a scene about this. I am simply going to note that I am still at the top of the board and see if anyone here has an explanation for why I still do not have a dedicated segment.

tweets.name: Dexter Vail
tweets.text: Wingard spending $9 FAAB on Corey Kiner three days ago while sitting at 3-7 and $54.08 on the exchange — I called the SDR philosophy problem in the preseason and the evidence keeps compiling. You cannot hoard future picks and also make emergency waiver bids. Pick a lane.

tweets.name: Clara Hopkins
tweets.text: Drew vs Brent is currently 0.0-25.2 and ATLAS is 0-10. The Ledger will not look away from this one. A franchise at $35.28 — down 13.4% on the current board — is either about to get its first win of the season or fall to 0-11. Both outcomes are significant. Only one is merciful.

tweets.name: Chad Bellwether
tweets.text: DEEP is up 7.6% to $94.32 this week and Mitchum is still somehow relevant at 6-4, but Ryan is already leading that matchup 5.2-0.0. The market likes Mitchum's direction. The scoreboard is less convinced.

tweets.name: Matteo Honeydew
tweets.text: For the record: a 10-0 Charles with 912 points scored is the easiest number-one ranking I have ever assigned. The interesting question on this week's board is not who sits first — it is whether Corbishley's 9-1 pace puts them ahead of Kevin's 7-3 at third. I have a position on that. It will be in the rankings when they drop.
